questions.questionText:
A car of mass 1,200 kg accelerates uniformly from 5 m/s to 25 m/s in 8.0 s along a level road.
(a) Calculate the acceleration of the car. [2 marks]
(b) Calculate the resultant forward force acting on the car. [2 marks]
(c) Calculate the distance travelled during these 8.0 s. [2 marks]

An electric pump raises 400 kg of water from a borehole 30 m deep to a raised tank in 40 s (g = 10 N/kg).
(a) Calculate the gravitational potential energy gained by the water. [2 marks]
(b) Calculate the useful power of the pump. [2 marks]
(c) If the electrical input power is 4.0 kW, calculate the percentage efficiency of the pump. [2 marks]

A block of metal of mass 2.0 kg and specific heat capacity 400 J/(kg°C) is heated from 20°C to 75°C by an electric immersion heater rated 500 W.
(a) Calculate the thermal energy absorbed by the metal block. [2 marks]
(b) Calculate the minimum time needed to heat the block assuming no heat loss. [2 marks]
(c) State why the actual time taken in a laboratory is longer. [1 mark]
questions.explanation:
(a) Q = mcΔθ = 2.0 × 400 × (75 - 20) = 44,000 J [2 marks].
(b) t = Q / P = 44,000 / 500 = 88 s [2 marks].
(c) Some heat is lost to the surrounding air, bench, and beaker [1 mark].

questions.questionText:
Two resistors of 4.0 Ω and 12.0 Ω are connected in parallel across a 12 V d.c. battery.
(a) Calculate the combined resistance of the two resistors. [2 marks]
(b) Calculate the total current drawn from the battery. [2 marks]
(c) Calculate the current flowing through the 4.0 Ω resistor. [2 marks]

(a) State the two conditions required for total internal reflection to occur. [2 marks]
(b) Glass has a refractive index n = 1.50. Calculate its critical angle c. [2 marks]
(c) Give one practical application of total internal reflection. [1 mark]
questions.explanation:
(a) Light travels from an optically denser to less dense medium, and angle of incidence exceeds critical angle (i > c) [2 marks].
(b) sin c = 1/n = 1/1.50 = 0.6667 -> c = 41.8° [2 marks].
(c) Optical fibres in telecommunications/endoscopes, or prism periscopes [1 mark].

questions.questionText:
A uniform beam AB of length 4.0 m and weight 100 N is pivoted at its midpoint C (2.0 m). A boy weighing 400 N sits 1.5 m from C on the left side.
(a) Calculate the anticlockwise moment produced by the boy about C. [2 marks]
(b) How far to the right of C must a girl weighing 300 N sit to balance the beam horizontally? [3 marks]
questions.explanation:
(a) Moment = F × d = 400 × 1.5 = 600 N·m [2 marks].
(b) Clockwise moment = 600 N·m -> 300 × d₂ = 600 -> d₂ = 2.0 m from C (at end B) [3 marks].

questions.questionText: Describe a simple laboratory experiment to determine the density of a small irregularly shaped stone using a balance and a measuring cylinder. [5 marks]
questions.explanation:
1. Measure mass m of the dry stone on an electronic/beam balance in grams [1 mark].
2. Pour water into a measuring cylinder and record initial volume V₁ [1 mark].
3. Tie stone with thin thread and gently lower until fully submerged; record new volume V₂ [1 mark].
4. Volume of stone V = V₂ - V₁ [1 mark].
5. Calculate density ρ = m / V [1 mark].

questions.questionText:
A transformer connected to 230 V mains supplies 11.5 V to a school bell.
(a) Explain why the transformer core is made of laminated soft iron. [2 marks]
(b) If the primary coil has 2,400 turns, calculate the number of turns on the secondary coil. [2 marks]
(c) If the secondary current is 2.0 A and the transformer is 100% efficient, find the primary current. [2 marks]
questions.explanation:
(a) Soft iron easily magnetises and demagnetises to link magnetic flux; laminations reduce eddy-current heating losses [2 marks].
(b) Ns = Np × (Vs/Vp) = 2400 × (11.5/230) = 120 turns [2 marks].
(c) VpIp = VsIs -> 230 × Ip = 11.5 × 2.0 -> Ip = 0.10 A [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A student fires a starting pistol 510 m from a cliff and hears the echo 3.0 s later.
(a) Calculate the speed of sound in air from these measurements. [3 marks]
(b) State two uses of ultrasound waves. [2 marks]
questions.explanation:
(a) Total distance travelled = 2 × 510 = 1,020 m [1 mark]. Speed = 1020 / 3.0 = 340 m/s [2 marks].
(b) Prenatal fetal imaging/scanning; cleaning delicate jewellery/instruments or sonar depth sounding [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
Compare alpha (α), beta (β), and gamma (γ) radiations in terms of:
(a) nature/identity [3 marks],
(b) ionising power and penetrating ability [3 marks],
(c) one safety precaution when handling radioactive sources in a school laboratory [1 mark].
questions.explanation:
(a) α: helium nucleus (2p+2n, charge +2); β: fast electron (-1); γ: high-frequency electromagnetic wave (0 charge) [3 marks].
(b) α is strongly ionising but stopped by paper; β has medium ionisation and is stopped by ~5 mm aluminium; γ is weakly ionising but highly penetrating requiring thick lead/concrete [3 marks].
(c) Handle with long tongs/forceps, keep sources in lead-lined box, never point at anyone [1 mark].

questions.questionText:
(a) Distinguish between evaporation and boiling of a liquid. Give two differences. [4 marks]
(b) Explain why a swimmer feels cold when stepping out of water into a breeze. [2 marks]
questions.explanation:
(a) Evaporation occurs at any temperature below boiling point and only at the surface; boiling occurs at a fixed temperature throughout the entire liquid with bubbles [4 marks].
(b) Breeze speeds evaporation; high-energy water molecules escape taking latent heat from the skin, lowering body surface temperature [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A car battery has an EMF of 12 V and delivers a current of 3.0 A to two identical headlamps connected in parallel.
(a) Explain what is meant by "EMF of 12 V". [2 marks]
(b) Calculate the total resistance of the two lamps combined and the resistance of a single lamp. [3 marks]
questions.explanation:
(a) 12 J of chemical energy is converted into electrical energy per coulomb of charge driven around the complete circuit [2 marks].
(b) R_total = V/I = 12/3.0 = 4.0 Ω [1 mark]. Since two identical lamps in parallel give half of one lamp: R_single = 2 × 4.0 = 8.0 Ω [2 marks].

questions.questionText: State Newton's three laws of motion and give one everyday example of Newton's First Law (inertia) in vehicle safety. [5 marks]
questions.explanation: 1st Law: A body stays at rest or constant velocity unless acted on by a resultant force [1]. 2nd Law: Resultant force F = ma (rate of change of momentum) [1]. 3rd Law: For every action force there is an equal and opposite reaction force [1]. Example: Seatbelts restrain passengers whose inertia tends to keep them moving forward when a car brakes suddenly [2].

questions.questionText:
A rectangular brick measures 20 cm × 10 cm × 5 cm and weighs 25 N.
(a) Calculate the maximum pressure it can exert on a table (in N/cm² and in Pa). [3 marks]
(b) Calculate the minimum pressure it can exert on the table (in N/cm²). [2 marks]
questions.explanation:
(a) Maximum pressure occurs on smallest area A = 10 × 5 = 50 cm² (= 0.005 m²). P_max = 25 / 50 = 0.50 N/cm² = 5,000 Pa [3 marks].
(b) Minimum pressure on largest area A = 20 × 10 = 200 cm². P_min = 25 / 200 = 0.125 N/cm² [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
(a) Draw/describe the truth table of a 2-input NOR gate. [2 marks]
(b) Explain how a thermistor can be used in a potential-divider circuit as an automatic fire alarm trigger. [3 marks]
questions.explanation:
(a) NOR gate outputs 1 ONLY when both inputs A=0 and B=0; outputs 0 when either or both inputs are 1 [2 marks].
(b) An NTC thermistor's resistance falls sharply as temperature rises; in series with a fixed resistor, voltage across the fixed resistor rises to exceed the threshold switching on the alarm/relay [3 marks].

questions.questionText: Describe an experiment to measure the specific heat capacity of water using an electrical immersion heater, thermometer, beaker, stopwatch, and joulemeter (or ammeter & voltmeter). [5 marks]
questions.explanation:
1. Weigh empty insulated beaker and add known mass m of water [1].
2. Record initial water temperature θ₁ [1].
3. Switch on heater, start stopwatch, and record V, I (or joulemeter reading E = VIt) while stirring gently [1].
4. Switch off, stir, and record highest steady temperature θ₂ [1].
5. Compute c = VIt / [m(θ₂ - θ₁)] [1].

questions.questionText:
An object 2.0 cm tall is placed 15 cm in front of a convex (converging) lens of focal length 10 cm.
(a) Use the lens formula 1/f = 1/u + 1/v to find the image distance v. [3 marks]
(b) State three properties of the image formed (real/virtual, upright/inverted, size). [3 marks]
questions.explanation:
(a) 1/10 = 1/15 + 1/v -> 1/v = 1/10 - 1/15 = 1/30 -> v = +30 cm [3 marks].
(b) Real, inverted, magnified (magnification = 30/15 = 2×, height 4.0 cm) [3 marks].

questions.questionText:
A copper rod rests across two bare horizontal rails inside a strong magnetic field directed vertically downwards. When a battery is connected across the rails, the rod rolls sideways.
(a) Name the physical effect demonstrated. [1 mark]
(b) State two ways to increase the force pushing the rod. [2 marks]
(c) State one way to reverse the direction of motion. [1 mark]
questions.explanation:
(a) The motor effect (force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field) [1 mark].
(b) Increase the electric current; use stronger magnets [2 marks].
(c) Reverse battery polarity (current direction) OR swap N and S magnetic poles [1 mark].

questions.questionText:
Explain why:
(a) small gaps are left between steel railway tracks, [2 marks]
(b) power lines hang loosely in summer, [2 marks]
(c) double-glazed windows keep rooms warmer in winter. [2 marks]
questions.explanation:
(a) Allows thermal expansion on hot sunny days so rails do not buckle/bend [2 marks].
(b) Prevents cables snapping under tension when they contract in cold winter nights [2 marks].
(c) Trapped dry air/vacuum between glass panes is a very poor conductor and suppresses convection currents [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A stone of mass 0.5 kg is thrown vertically upwards at 20 m/s (g = 10 m/s²). Neglecting air resistance:
(a) Calculate its initial kinetic energy. [2 marks]
(b) Use conservation of energy to calculate the maximum height reached. [3 marks]
questions.explanation:
(a) KE = ½mv² = ½ × 0.5 × 20² = 100 J [2 marks].
(b) At max height all KE converts to GPE: mgh = 100 -> 0.5 × 10 × h = 100 -> h = 20 m [3 marks].
